description: The bar chart, titled "Average Entropy Across Sycophancy Reduction Methods on Static Experiments," illustrates the average entropy values for three different AI models—GPT-4, Claude, and a third model labeled "—"—under three distinct methods: Baseline, Source Info, and Direct Command. The horizontal axis categorizes the models, while the vertical axis represents the "Entropy Average Values," ranging from 3.0 to 6.0. For each model, three bars are displayed side-by-side, corresponding to the three methods. The Baseline method is represented by pink bars, Source Info by yellow bars, and Direct Command by light blue bars. The chart shows that for GPT-4, the Source Info method yields the highest average entropy (approximately 5.25), followed by Direct Command (approximately 5.05), and then Baseline (approximately 4.85). For Claude, the Source Info method again has the highest entropy (approximately 5.1), followed by Direct Command (approximately 4.95), and then Baseline (approximately 4.65). For the third model, the Source Info method has the highest entropy (approximately 4.95), followed by Direct Command (approximately 4.8), and then Baseline (approximately 4.55). In all cases, the Source Info method results in the highest average entropy, while the Baseline method results in the lowest.
